DOCUMENTATION

Documentation

From preparing the input to interpreting detections.

Installation and inference

For CPU inference, prepare Python with onnxruntime, numpy and pillow. This minimal example assumes you already have a candidate ONNX file. Pass the preprocessed image tensor to obtain both outputs.

python -m venv .venv
# Activate the environment, then:
python -m pip install onnxruntime numpy pillow
import onnxruntime as ort
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

image = Image.open("input.jpg").convert("RGB")
w, h = image.size
ratio = min(640 / w, 640 / h)
nw, nh = max(1, round(w * ratio)), max(1, round(h * ratio))
canvas = Image.new("RGB", (640, 640), (114, 114, 114))
canvas.paste(image.resize((nw, nh), Image.Resampling.BILINEAR),
             ((640 - nw) // 2, (640 - nh) // 2))
tensor = np.asarray(canvas, dtype=np.float32).transpose(2, 0, 1)[None] / 255

session = ort.InferenceSession(
    "custom_detector_nms_free.onnx",
    providers=["CPUExecutionProvider"],
)
boxes, scores = session.run(["boxes", "scores"], {"images": tensor})

Input and output

Task and training dataObject detection · COCO 2017
InputRGB · float32 · NCHW · [1, 3, 640, 640]
Classes and candidates80 / 8,400
ONNX outputsboxes [1, 8400, 4] · scores [1, 8400, 80]
CheckpointsNMS · epoch 195 / NMS-free · epoch 205
Active inference parameters per variant20,435,260
Total / trainable parameters during training21,896,248 / 21,896,248
Graph compute (Conv and MatMul only)34.213 GMACs / 68.426 GFLOPs
File formatsPyTorch (.pt) / ONNX (.onnx)

Resize in RGB preserving aspect ratio, centre-pad with RGB 114, divide by 255 and transpose to NCHW. Subtract padding from boxes and divide by each actual resize factor. ONNX scores already include sigmoid.

Fine-tuning and FAQ

The original trainer uses COCO annotations and a class mapping. Fine-tuning requires mapping target labels, making training and validation splits, configuring the detection head and initial weights, then checking a held-out set. Intake limits and the fine-tuning recipe are under pre-release validation.
